version.changelog: Unify CLI parameters, streamline the skill, and add first-run defaults with recommended setup.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.1.8

The skill bundle contains high-risk capabilities, most notably the ability to execute arbitrary commands on remote hosts via SSH if a specific environment variable is set (run.sh). Additionally, SKILL.md explicitly instructs the AI agent to bypass the isolated 'openclaw' browser profile and use the user's primary Chrome environment, which grants access to the user's active sessions and cookies. While these features appear intended to facilitate web scraping on platforms like TikTok and Amazon, the combination of remote execution, local bridge command execution (collect_and_export_loop.sh), and the bypass of browser isolation represents a significant security risk without further sandboxing.

llm.summary: The skill's scripts and instructions match a browser-bridge web-collection tool, but several choices could expose broad user data or execute arbitrary commands/remote runs unless carefully constrained.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (browser-plugin collection via a local bridge) match the included scripts. Required binaries curl and node are used by the scripts and are proportionate to the task.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts explicitly instruct using the user's normal Chrome environment (not an isolated profile), access a local bridge API (default http://127.0.0.1:19820), and run a bundled closed-loop collector. Using the user's normal browser risks collecting unrelated private data. The flow allows the agent to start a bridge by running an arbitrary BRIDGE_CMD (nohup bash -lc "$BRIDGE_CMD"), and the run wrapper supports remote execution (WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH) — both expand runtime authority beyond simple collection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) and included files are local shell/node scripts. Nothing is downloaded or extracted from remote URLs by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required credentials, which matches the manifest, but it relies on optional env vars and stored preferences that can point the bridge to arbitrary endpoints (WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL / defaultBridgeUrl) or run arbitrary commands (WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_CMD). If those values point to remote hosts or untrusted commands, collected data could be forwarded externally or arbitrary code could be started.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced global installation). The skill writes only its own preference file under OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or $HOME/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json, which is expected for local state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to be what it claims (a local browser-plugin collector) but contains a few risky design choices you should consider before installing: 

- Privacy: it tells the agent to use your normal Chrome profile (not an isolated profile), so if you run it it could interact with cookies, logged-in sessions, or other browsing data beyond the target sites. Prefer running in an isolated/profile or test environment.
- Bridge URL and exports: the bridge base URL (WEB_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_URL or stored defaultBridgeUrl) can be set to any server. Ensure it points to a trusted local bridge (127.0.0.1) — otherwise collected data could be sent to a remote host.
- Arbitrary command execution: the --ensure-bridge flow will run BRIDGE_CMD with nohup bash -lc. Only enable --ensure-bridge if you control and trust BRIDGE_CMD. Avoid untrusted BRIDGE_CMD values.
- Remote execution: the runner supports remote SSH (WEB_COLLECTION_REMOTE_SSH); do not enable this unless you expect remote collection and trust the remote host.

Recommended actions: review the scripts locally, run them in an isolated environment, verify preference file contents (especially defaultBridgeUrl), avoid --ensure-bridge and remote SSH unless you control the bridge/host, and prefer an isolated browser profile to limit exposure.
